newsitem.title: GERMANY: Krupp says Dortmund furnace won't be closed.
newsitem.headline: Krupp says Dortmund furnace won't be closed.

text.p: Krupp will not close at least part of its Dortmund steel plant if its steel operations are merged with those of Thyssen AG, Krupp personnel director Juergen Rossberg told a gathering of steel workers on Thursday.
"A closing of the liquid stage (blast furnace and steel works) here will not happen with me," Rossberg said, adding he spoke also in the name of Krupp chairman Gerhard Cromme.
Rossberg made no comment on Krupp's hot rolling mill also located in Dortmund.
Analysts have speculated Krupp's Dortmund works would be the most likely target for rationalisation in the event of a merger, as the Krupp plant is less modern than Thyssen facilities.
The management board of Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp believes it will take at least six months to work out a viable plan for a fusion of the two companies' steel operations, Rossberg said.
In the event of a merger, the negative consequences such as job cuts must be shared fairly between the two companies, Rossberg said.
Krupp on Tuesday launched a hostile takeover bid for its larger rival Thyssen, but that attack is on hold for eight days while the two discuss a possible fusion of their steel operations.
